subject: Mariner Health - Private/VPC discovery recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@marinerhealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@marinerhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -04:00
Subject: Mariner Health - Private/VPC discovery recap

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. As promised, below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria, and next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points / goals
- Regulated PHI workloads (HIPAA) with strict audit and data-residency requirements.
- Current LLM experiments are running in a prototype on EKS in a restricted VPC; they cannot send PHI to public SaaS endpoints.
- Need support for customer-managed keys (BYOK) + HSM integration for encryption at rest and auditability.
- For some workloads (batch inference and model updates) they may require an air-gapped/on-prem option.
- Network constraints: limited or no outbound internet from the VPC; strict egress rules and force traffic through company proxies.

Current stack (what we heard)
- AWS (GovCloud region for production), EKS for orchestration, on-prem data lake for records.
- Prototype uses a small in-house LLM endpoint (latency varies), team testing embeddings + chat for triage workflows.

Success criteria (initial POC)
- Private deployment with VPC peering or customer-managed VPC (no PHI to public inference endpoints).
- BYOK with HSM/KMS integration and audit logs accessible to their compliance team.
- Ability to run with no external egress for a subset of workloads (air-gapped option or secure bulk transfer process).
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile < 300ms for short-chat endpoints (or agreed ramp), predictable throughput for batch jobs (peak TPS estimate needed).

Risks / open questions
- Full air-gap vs staged transfer approach for model updates (need to understand CI/CD constraints).
- Certification artifacts required by their procurement team (SOC2, penetration test summary).
- Exact HSM vendor and integration method (KMIP vs cloud KMS gateway).

Attachments shared (attached to this email)
- redwood-private-overview.pdf (high-level architecture and deployment options)
- SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf (recent attestation summary)
- network-checklist.xlsx (initial network requirements checklist for your infra team)

Next steps / action items
1) Marissa (me) to share the attachments and a short FAQ on BYOK/HSM integration (today).
2) Samantha to share the approximate peak capacity (requests/sec) and an infra contact for the technical deep-dive (this week).
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Redwood infra + their security/infra engineers (target week of Jul 27).
4) Redwood to provide a short options matrix: Dedicated vs Private (on-prem) with rough timelines and POC checklist.

Planned attendees for technical deep-dive (please confirm):
- From Mariner Health: their infra/security lead (TBD)
- From Redwood: Aditya Rao (Solutions Architect), Rishi Malhotra (Security/Compliance)

Thanks — I’ll follow up shortly with the documents and a Calendly for the tech call.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Mariner Health - Private/VPC discovery recap

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- For BYOK/HSM: we use an on-prem HSM (Thales) currently and will need to understand if Redwood can either integrate with our HSM via KMIP gateway or accept wrapped keys in a transfer process. We can provide the HSM contact for the technical call.
- Air-gap: ideally we’d avoid frequent full air-gap model pulls. We’re open to a staged approach where model binaries are transferred via encrypted media and validated in a sealed environment. We’ll detail our CI/CD process for model updates in the tech deep-dive.
- Data residency: production will live in AWS GovCloud (US). Any audit logs we need to retain locally for 7 years — we’ll bring the retention requirements to the call.

Action from our side: I’ll get the infra/security contact and peak TPS estimates by Thursday. Also attaching a short internal network policy excerpt that may be helpful.

Appreciate the quick follow-up — Samantha

Samantha Lee
VP, Engineering Operations | Mariner Health

Excellent — thanks Samantha. Looping in the folks who will run the technical deep-dive: Aditya (solutions architecture) and Rishi (security/compliance).

Aditya / Rishi — quick context: Mariner Health is evaluating Private/VPC deployment for PHI workloads in AWS GovCloud. Key asks: BYOK + HSM integration (Thales), optional air-gapped model update process, strict egress rules (no external internet for some subnets), and 7-year local audit log retention. They will provide an infra/security contact and peak TPS by Thursday.

Proposed next moves for Redwood ops:
- Aditya: please review the attached network checklist and confirm what we need from Mariner to validate a Private deployment (VPC peering vs customer-managed VPC, proxy/gateway config, ports, and proxies).
- Rishi: please prepare the SOC2/penetration test artifacts we can share with procurement and outline the HSM integration options (KMIP gateway, wrapped-key workflow, or cloud KMS bridge).
- I’ll send a calendar invite for a 60-min tech deep-dive — suggested slots Wed Jul 29 10am PT or Thu Jul 30 2pm PT; Samantha, let us know which works for your team.

Samantha — will also share the options matrix (Dedicated vs Private vs On-prem) and an initial POC timeline by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks all — look forward to the next call.
